components.description: Federal FMLA leave as administered by Georgia Tech Policy 2.12 and BOR Policy 8.2.7.6: up to 12 workweeks of unpaid, job-protected leave in a rolling 12-month period for the birth or adoption/foster placement of a child (and for a serious health condition of the employee or a spouse, child or parent). Accrued sick leave and/or vacation must be used concurrently before unpaid status; bonding leave must be continuous and within 12 months of the birth or placement.
components.faculty_group_note: GT Policy 2.12 scope: 'All faculty and staff within the Georgia Institute of Technology'; BOR 8.2.7.6 applies to USG employees.

components.dual_employee_rule: spouses both working for the University System of Georgia and FMLA-eligible: combined total of 12 workweeks in any 12-month period for birth or placement
components.entitlement_note: Statutory entitlement; GT 2.12: 'entitles eligible employees to take up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job protected leave'.
components.duration_note: BOR 8.2.7.6 'up to twelve (12) work weeks'; GT 2.12 'up to 12 weeks'; rolling 12-month period. Statute: 29 U.S.C. 2612(a)(1).
components.time_window: bonding leave within the 12 months immediately following the birth, adoption, or placement, taken as a single continuous period (not intermittent)

components.relief_note: A leave of absence; relief not stated (R9).

notes: Reference date 2018-02-22. 2018_10 is the Feb 2018 Faculty Handbook; 2018_11 is the Oct 2016 Faculty Handbook, which differs from 2018_10 in the table of contents, page footers, numbering and the 3.3.5 differences.

Governing documents: GT Policies 2.11 Leave of Absence, 2.12 Family Leave (FMLA) and 2.13 Sick Leave (HR policy library, last revised Oct 2014, review date Oct 2017; scope all faculty and staff); the Faculty Handbook (Feb 2018 edition; 3.1.4 leave policies, 3.3.3 and 3.3.5 tenure clock), which defers to the USG Board of Regents Policy Manual 8.2.7 and the Academic and Student Affairs Handbook 4.9; the ASMD program document dated Nov 27, 2017 with its web page and request form. Georgia Tech has no paid parental leave and no paid maternity leave in these documents: GT 2.11 'Maternity Leave' says 'Appropriate sick leave provisions shall apply' (coded within c2). Faculty are not unionised (version note).

Edition question (version note): the Feb 2018 Handbook's day of effect is unknown; the Oct 2016 edition differs for parents only in 3.3.5 (adoption limited to a child under six; requests within three months instead of twelve; 'part-time service' instead of 'alternative service'; leave 'approved by the President'). Components resting on those differences (c7, c8) are flagged version_uncertain; c6's substance is the same in both editions and in BOR 8.3.7.4.

Vacation: academic-year (9-month) faculty, the standard tenure-stream appointment, do not earn vacation (BOR 8.2.7.1), so the vacation route for bonding (c3) is open only to 12-month faculty; sick leave may not be used for bonding with a healthy newborn. A 9-month faculty member's FMLA bonding leave is therefore unpaid unless ASMD (relief, not leave) is used.

Birth parent chain: FMLA 12 workweeks (c1), with own sick leave (c2), vacation if any (c3) and STD benefits if insured (c10) used within it → sick leave without pay up to one year after FMLA (c4, discretionary), all leaves combined capped at 12 months; ASMD course release (c9, discretionary) also available in up to two semesters within twelve months of the birth; tenure-clock suspension during the leave (c6) and extension (c7).

Non-birth parent chain: FMLA 12 workweeks (c1; sick leave c2 only for care of an ill spouse, vacation c3 if a 12-month appointee) → ASMD one-course release in one semester (c9, discretionary) also available; tenure-clock suspension (c6) and extension (c7). Spouses both employed by the USG share a combined 12 workweeks of FMLA for a birth.

Calendar: semesters ('academic year of two semesters'; 'only fall and spring semesters for nine-month faculty'); no length stated, so calendar.kind = semester, and the term length follows R8's order. The '39 week academic year' in 5.6.5 is a consulting-limit construct, not a term length.

Leaves considered and not coded (cannot be used for a birth): educational and professional leave with or without pay (scholarly purposes only; BOR 8.2.7.4, ASA Handbook 4.9.2, Handbook 3.1.4 'Leave of Absence with Pay'); study leave/sabbatical (Handbook 5.6.5); military leave; court duty; voting; military physical; blood, organ and marrow donation; bereavement; education support leave (8 hours a year for student-achievement activities); emergency/inclement-weather leave.

Cited but not saved: FMLA FAQ Index and Benefits Forms (GT 2.12); Leave of Absence Request Form, USG Time Away from Work Educational Leave Policy and Military Leave Policy (GT 2.11); Board of Regents HR Administrative Practice Manual sections on Sick Leave with Pay and without Pay, GT Vacation and Sick Leave Request Form (GT 2.13); a 'Donated Sick Leave' policy listed in the GT Policy Library navigation; the short-term disability insurance plan; Disability Services (ASMD page); BOR Policy Manual sections 3.2.1-3.2.3 (faculty definitions), Academic Affairs Handbook Section 4.0 contract forms, BOR Bylaws Article VIII, Library Faculty Constitution, Anti-Harassment Policy, Student Rules and Regulations (Handbook); the Faculty Affairs web site forms for probationary extension.

One-meaning check: c6 (suspension of the clock during a birth or adoption leave), c7 (one-year extension for compelling circumstances) and c8 (interruption for any leave) are separate provisions of the same Handbook section, split because they differ in trigger and purpose.
